transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi. Uh... well, I guess for the past year or so, I've just been having some trouble at work. Getting pulled off what I'm doing. 

It's just... small things, really. A phone buzzing, somebody walking past my office. Sometimes even just a random thought about my in-laws, things like that. It just takes me away from what I'm doing before I can stop it. Figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
When your mind gets pulled away like that, are you often caught up in worrying about things—like your health, work, or family—that feels hard to control?

Uh... no. Not really. 

I don't... I'm not sitting there stressing about my health or whatever. It's just a random thought. Doesn't mean I'm worried about it. It just distracts me, that's all.
Have you always had trouble staying focused like this since you were a kid, or is this something new that started more recently?

Yeah... I guess it's not really new. Looking back, it was kind of like this when I was a kid, too. 

School was... well, teachers were always moving my seat around. Said I talked too much, or I'd just get up without asking. Or I'd blurt things out before they even finished the question. Stuff like that. So... yeah. Always been there, I suppose.
These days, do you still notice things like feeling restless, interrupting others, or acting impulsively before thinking things through?

Yeah, I guess. Mostly just... cutting people off, maybe. 

I don't really mean to. Just... if an employee is talking, sometimes I'll just finish their thought for them before they're done. Or, uh, if my wife is talking to her parents, I kind of just jump into the conversation. 

I can tell it rubs people the wrong way sometimes, but... yeah. I do that.
